newsitem.title: USA: Repression dooms Milosevic dream of West - Christopher.
newsitem.headline: Repression dooms Milosevic dream of West - Christopher.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher on Wednesday warned Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic that continuing his "repressive, undemocratic stance" would doom his dreams of ties to the West.

Interviewed on CBS This Morning from Brussels, Belgium, where he was attending the meeting of NATO foreign ministers, Christopher said the Serbian leader "is turning his back on opportunities to join the West."
Christopher said NATO had sent a strong message to Milosevic on Tuesday that he "should hear the voices of the Serbian people, the Yugoslav people, he should understand their votes."
Hundreds of thousands of Serbians have been protesting daily against Milosevic's refusal to allow opposition officials elected last month to take control of the local Belgrade government.
The opposition lost a legal battle on Tuesday when the Yugoslav supreme court refused to hear its claim of electoral fraud by the ruling socialists.

Christopher said the NATO message warned Milosevic that "he would not be able to fulfil his dreams of joining the Western European countries so long as he pursues this repressive, undemocratic stance."
"He really is turning his back on opportunities to join the West, which I know is important to him."
Christopher said the United States was considering economic sanctions. The United Nations imposed sanctions imposed on Yugoslavia for 3-1/2 years during the war in Bosnia.

"I think he desires full and normal relations with the United States. We're going to continue withholding that until we see signs on his part that he's prepared to have a democratic, open society," Christopher said.
